entities.name: HIV-1 Env gp160
observations: 768-aa sequence has 74.2–74.7% identity and 100% query coverage to reviewed HIV-1 group M Env gp160 proteins.
Contains Pfam GP120 domains at positions 36–142 and 150–500, plus GP41 domain at positions 519–709.
N-terminal signal peptide is predicted by close homolog feature mapping; the mature precursor is glycosylated and furin-cleaved into gp120 and gp41.
Architecture is a type-I viral envelope protein: large extracellular gp120 region, one C-terminal transmembrane helix, and cytoplasmic gp41 tail.
Sequence-derived properties: molecular weight approximately 86.8 kDa, theoretical pI 8.59, and predicted positive charge at neutral pH.

entities.name: HIV-1 gp120
observations: Surface subunit generated by furin-like cleavage of Env gp160.
Mediates attachment to CD4 and subsequent engagement of CCR5 or CXCR4 coreceptors according to reviewed homolog annotations.
Forms a noncovalent heterodimer with gp41 within trimeric Env spikes.

entities.name: HIV-1 gp41
observations: Transmembrane subunit generated by furin-like cleavage of Env gp160.
Contains the fusion peptide and membrane-proximal fusion machinery; acts as a class-I viral membrane-fusion protein according to reviewed homolog annotations.
Anchors Env in the virion membrane through a single transmembrane helix and includes a cytoplasmic tail.

entities.name: HIV entry and membrane fusion
observations: Env mediates virion attachment to host cells, receptor-triggered conformational change, and fusion of viral and host membranes.
Annotated processes include fusion with host plasma or endosomal membranes and clathrin-dependent viral endocytosis.

entities.name: Virion membrane
observations: Env is localized to the viral envelope/virion membrane and is also present at host plasma and endosomal membranes during entry.
